comments.text: Hi Zac - love your channel. I'm in Guatemala on vacation; I decided to use Uber Eats to get myself and two sisters, mom, some lunch and also maybe have some leftovers later for tomorrow (or for my cousins should they stop by later tonight to hang out). So I ordered a large house special fried rice, large house special chow mein (both, btw, come in tub of butter sized containers, something like maybe three or four of the typical Chinese restaurant rice containers, a ton of food), a large order of shrimp wontons (they sent over 20, each the size of two typical fried wontons in New York); and a large order of egg rolls (again, each one being twice the size of a regular egg role from a NYC Chinese joint, and 10 of them total). Three cans of soda added in, total was... $35.00. With a 20% tip. Now, I know that we're in a country that's not America, but JFC, I figured this would be at least $70, maybe $80 in a typical US Chinese restaurant. I am baffled (but also extremely grateful) to be able to feed something like 10 people on $35, where in New York (where I was born and live/work) I wouldn't even invite 1 friend anywhere due to the high prices on food.

They have the tools to cook at home now, and if you're into that disgusting pre-made meal delivery service nonsense, good for you, but I'm just letting you know it's still going to be cheaper making your own food at the end of the day (plus you'll be throwing away way less packaging.) Ultimately you have signed on for a tv dinner delivery service 😂

comments.author: @cassiegreene9528
comments.text: People! Pack your lunch. They make all these nifty divided containers so you can put all kinds of things in them. And putting your own food together is rather fun. I'm old now and I had to take Home Economics in high school - great class as I learned basic cooking (muffins were our first assignment...) Nowadays YouTube can teach you how to cook. Don't give these corporate restaurants a-holes your hard earned money. And it's very easy to grow a tomato in a pot.

comments.author: @TimidLecher
comments.text: I love my boyfriend, we've been together going on 20 years, but he knows I am not into marriage. The other week he casually mentioned that we should get hitched, move somewhere, and he could try to open his own restaurant (he's a chef.) My response: "no, if you open a restaurant and we're married then I will inherit your debt if it fails. Wouldn't it make sense for one of us to keep good credit just in case the other goes into debt?" And I firmly believe what I said, because MOST RESTAURANTS FAIL. It's an unforgiving industry where everyone is miserable. Count me out.
